newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Port strike slashes Swedish iron ore shipments.
newsitem.headline: Port strike slashes Swedish iron ore shipments.

text.p: A three-week strike by Norwegian port workers has slashed daily shipments by two-thirds from an iron ore mine in northern Sweden, a spokesman for Swedish state-owned miner LKAB said on Thursday.

Daily shipments of finished products from LKAB's mine in Kiruna were about 20,000 tonnes, down from 60,000 tonnes, since workers in the port of Narvik went on strike on September 26, LKAB spokesman Raymond Hedman said.
Some shipments are continuing to go through the northern Swedish port of Lulea.
LKAB has lost customers because of the drop in shipments and shortfall in supplies, Hedman said.
"The longer the strike, the larger the risk that more customers will turn to other suppliers. We have very strong competitors from Brazil, Australia and Canada," he said.
He said LKAB was stockpiling some iron ore to absorb disruption caused by the strike.
The port workers, LKAB employees who load ships, have demanded the retirement age be lowered to 55 from 62, he said.
A government-appointed mediator had been called in to help resolve the conflict and a new round of talks are due to begin next week, Hedman said.
Lulea cannot handle ships as large as Narvik could, meaning higher shipping costs in smaller vessels would be passed on to customers, Hedman said.
LKAB ships roughly 15 million tonnes of iron ore products annually through Narvik. --Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003
